stem:
Rohit holds a bamboo stick and a steel spoon of about the same size; the steel spoon feels heavier. Later he sees a piece of ice floating on liquid water.

Which claim best explains floating or sinking here?

options.text: Density can differ even when size is the same; ice is lighter than liquid water, so the ice floats.
The steel spoon feels heavier only because it is larger than the bamboo stick.
Ice floats because it is heavier than liquid water.
Any object that feels heavy must sink in liquid water, even if its density is low.

teacher.key_rationale: Same-size objects can differ in density; floating and sinking depend on material density, not size or apparent heaviness alone. Ice is less dense than liquid water, so it floats.
